correctness.rationale: The finite theorem is completely verified. I independently enumerated all \(512\) matrices in \(M_3(\mathbb F_2)\) and found exactly \(64\) nilpotents including zero. The displayed six-space has \(64\) elements and meets the nonzero nilpotent set trivially. I then independently enumerated all \({9\brack3}_2=788035\) three-dimensional orthogonal complements and obtained exactly \(128\) nilpotent-free six-spaces; conjugation by all \(168\) elements of \(\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb F_2)\) partitions them into orbits of sizes \(8,8,56,56\), with the displayed witness in a size-\(56\) orbit. This is exhaustive finite proof, not sampling.
residual_risks: The theorem is only for \((\mathbb F_2,3)\); it does not prove the finite-field conjecture uniformly.
